claim: Exosomes are 30–150 nm vesicles formed by inward budding of the limiting membrane of late endosomes to produce multivesicular bodies (MVBs) that contain intraluminal vesicles (ILVs).
source: Exosomes are 30–150 nm vesicles formed by inward budding of the limiting membrane of late endosomes to produce multivesicular bodies (MVBs) that contain intraluminal vesicles (ILVs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about exosome biogenesis, supported by citation to Harding et al., 1983 in the following sentence.

claim: Upon fusion of MVBs with the plasma membrane, ILVs are released to the extracellular space as exosomes.
source: Upon fusion of MVBs with the plasma membrane, ILVs are released to the extracellular space as exosomes (Harding et al., 1983).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Harding et al., 1983.

claim: Elevation of cytosolic Ca2+ with ionophores induces rapid exosome secretion in a Rab27a, Munc13-4-dependent manner.
source: Interestingly, elevation of cytosolic Ca2+ with ionophores has been demonstrated to induce rapid exosome secretion in a Rab27a, Munc13-4-dependent manner (Messenger et al., 2018; Savina et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Messenger et al., 2018 and Savina et al., 2003.

claim: Perforation of the plasma membrane results in an influx of extracellular Ca2+ into the cytoplasm and triggers a repair cascade that includes mobilization and fusion of lysosomes with the plasma membrane.
source: Perforation of the plasma membrane results in an influx of extracellular Ca2+ into the cytoplasm and triggers a repair cascade that includes mobilization and fusion of lysosomes with the plasma membrane (Andrews and Corrotte, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Andrews and Corrotte, 2018.

claim: Some reports have suggested that, unlike lysosomes, MVBs do not undergo Ca2+-dependent exocytosis.
source: However, some reports have suggested that, unlike lysosomes, MVBs do not undergo Ca2+-dependent exocytosis (Jaiswal et al., 2004; Jaiswal et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jaiswal et al., 2004 and Jaiswal et al., 2002.

claim: Furimazine permeates through cellular membranes and enables luminescence from both cellular debris and intact CD63-Nluc exosomes present within the conditioned medium of cultured CD63-Nluc cells.
source: Furimazine, the substrate of Nluc, permeates through cellular membranes and enables luminescence from both cellular debris and intact CD63-Nluc exosomes present within the conditioned medium of cultured CD63-Nluc cells.
evidence: This is a description of the assay design based on the known properties of furimazine.

claim: The addition of a membrane-impermeable Nluc inhibitor eliminates luminescence derived from cellular debris where Nluc is readily accessible, while not affecting the luminescence derived from intact CD63-Nluc exosomes incubated with furimazine.
source: The addition of a membrane-impermeable Nluc inhibitor eliminates luminescence derived from cellular debris where Nluc is readily accessible, while not affecting the luminescence derived from intact CD63-Nluc exosomes incubated with furimazine (Walker et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Walker et al., 2017.

claim: The addition of the membrane-impermeable Nluc inhibitor depleted approximately 30% of luminescence derived from the conditioned medium of CD63-Nluc cells.
source: The addition of the membrane-impermeable Nluc inhibitor depleted a significant portion of luminescence derived from the conditioned medium of CD63-Nluc cells (~30%) and membrane solubilization by TX-100 reduced luminescence to background levels (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Membrane solubilization by TX-100 reduced luminescence to background levels.
source: The addition of the membrane-impermeable Nluc inhibitor depleted a significant portion of luminescence derived from the conditioned medium of CD63-Nluc cells (~30%) and membrane solubilization by TX-100 reduced luminescence to background levels (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: CD63-Nluc luminescence was removed after high-speed sedimentation or upon the addition of TX-100.
source: To further validate the localization of the CD63-Nluc luminescence signal to sedimentable vesicles, we subjected the conditioned medium fraction to differential centrifugation and found that CD63-Nluc luminescence was removed after high-speed sedimentation or upon the addition of TX-100 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: CD63-Nluc vesicles equilibrated at a density of 1.11 g/ml on a linear iodixanol gradient.
source: CD63-Nluc vesicles equilibrated at a density of 1.11 g/ml, a buoyancy similar to published reports (Jeppesen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data (Figure 1D) and comparison to published reports (Jeppesen et al., 2019).

claim: Secreted CD63-Nluc luminescence increased linearly over 24 hr.
source: In a time course over 24 hr, we measured secreted CD63-Nluc luminescence in the presence of Nluc inhibitor alone or with TX-100 and found the signal increased linearly, consistent with exosome secretion over time (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Influx of Ca2+ into the cytoplasm using the Ca2+ ionophore ionomycin (5 µM, 30 min) induced robust exosome secretion compared to the level of secretion of the vehicle control.
source: In agreement with previous reports (Messenger et al., 2018), influx of Ca2+ into the cytoplasm using the Ca2+ ionophore ionomycin (5 µM, 30 min) induced robust exosome secretion compared to the level of secretion of the vehicle control (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and citation to Messenger et al., 2018.

claim: Exosome secretion initiated within 2 min of ionomycin treatment and was complete by 10 min.
source: Exosome secretion initiated within 2 min of ionomycin treatment and was complete by 10 min (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Treatment with 400 ng/ml or 800 ng/ml of SLO significantly increased exosome production, dependent on the presence of extracellular CaCl2 (1.8 mM).
source: Treatment with 400 ng/ml or 800 ng/ml of SLO significantly increased exosome production, dependent on the presence of extracellular CaCl2 (1.8 mM).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: SLO induced exosome secretion 2 min after initial application and was complete after 10–20 min.
source: Similar to ionomycin, SLO induced exosome secretion 2 min after initial application and was complete after 10–20 min (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Application of a physiological mechanical stress induced exosome secretion in a Ca2+-dependent manner.
source: Application of a physiological mechanical stress also induced exosome secretion in a Ca2+-dependent manner (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: A 30 min ionomycin treatment induced the secretion of low-buoyant density, ANXA2- and FLOT2-positive vesicles compared to the 24 hr vehicle control.
source: A 30 min ionomycin treatment induced the secretion of low-buoyant density, ANXA2- and FLOT2-positive vesicles (Figure 2F, Fraction #8) compared to the 24 hr vehicle control.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: CD63 and Nluc signals equilibrated to higher buoyant density fractions corresponding to the position expected for exosomes.
source: Alternatively, CD63 and Nluc signals equilibrated to higher buoyant density fractions corresponding to the position expected for exosomes (Figure 2F, Fraction #10).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Treatment with nocodazole, a microtubule polymerization inhibitor, but not latrunculin A, an actin polymerization inhibitor, reduced vehicle- and ionomycin-induced exosome secretion.
source: Treatment with nocodazole, a microtubule polymerization inhibitor, but not latrunculin A, an actin polymerization inhibitor, reduced vehicle- and ionomycin-induced exosome secretion (Figure 2H, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: The 0.2% TX-100 elution fractions were significantly enriched in LAMP1 and diminished in GAPDH compared to the input, regardless of the presence of CaCl2 or EGTA in the elution.
source: The 0.2% TX-100 elution fractions were significantly enriched in LAMP1 and diminished in GAPDH compared to the input, regardless of the presence of CaCl2 or EGTA in the elution (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A gel stained for total protein showed four intense protein bands unique to the EGTA-eluted sample.
source: A gel stained for total protein showed four intense protein bands unique to the EGTA-eluted sample (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Mass spectrometry identified annexin A6 (ANXA6) and copine 3 (CPNE3) in the upper gel slice, annexin A2 (ANXA2) in the middle gel slice, and S100 Ca2+-binding protein A10 (S100A10) in the lower gel slice.
source: We identified annexin A6 (ANXA6) and copine 3 (CPNE3) in the upper gel slice, annexin A2 (ANXA2) in the middle gel slice, and S100 Ca2+-binding protein A10 (S100A10) in the lower gel slice.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Knockdown of ANXA6 and CPNE3 decreased Ca2+-dependent exosome secretion relative to a GFP knockdown control.
source: However, we were able to efficiently knock down ANXA6 and CPNE3 with two different shRNAs (Figure 4A and B), and in each case, Ca2+-dependent exosome secretion decreased relative to a GFP knockdown control (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, B, C, and D.

claim: One of the ANXA6 shRNAs slightly decreased constitutive exosome secretion relative to the GFP control.
source: One of the ANXA6 shRNAs also slightly decreased constitutive exosome secretion relative to the GFP control, although the effect was relatively small (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: A polyclonal knockout of ANXA6 decreased exosome secretion relative to a non-targeting control.
source: A polyclonal knockout of ANXA6 also decreased exosome secretion relative to a non-targeting control (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: An accumulation of CD63-positive vesicles at the cell periphery was observed, particularly in ionomycin-treated ANXA6 knockdown cells.
source: We observed an accumulation of CD63-positive vesicles at the cell periphery, particularly in ionomycin-treated ANXA6 knockdown cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Addition of either rat liver cytosol or Ca2+ promoted exosome secretion slightly and the addition of both rat liver cytosol and Ca2+ promoted exosome secretion ~12-fold over the control condition.
source: We observed that addition of either rat liver cytosol or Ca2+ promoted exosome secretion slightly and that the addition of both rat liver cytosol and Ca2+ promoted exosome secretion ~12-fold over the control condition (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The addition of HCT116 WT cytosol and Ca2+ promoted exosome secretion ~15-fold over the control condition.
source: The addition of HCT116 WT cytosol and Ca2+ promoted exosome secretion ~15-fold over the control condition (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The Ca2+-only reaction was stimulated by the addition of the ATPr and GTP, whereas the stimulatory effect obtained with cytosol alone appeared to be nucleotide-independent.
source: We observed that the Ca2+-only reaction was stimulated by the addition of the ATPr and GTP (columns 3 and 7), whereas the stimulatory effect obtained with cytosol alone appeared to be nucleotide-independent (columns 2 and 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Addition of an anti-GFP antibody slightly decreased exosome secretion whereas the equivalent addition of an anti-ANXA6 antibody decreased exosome secretion to a background level seen in a reaction without added cytosol.
source: Addition of an anti-GFP antibody slightly decreased exosome secretion whereas the equivalent addition of an anti-ANXA6 antibody (whose specificity was validated by immunoblot analysis in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) decreased exosome secretion to a background level seen in a reaction without added cytosol (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: ANXA6(FL) maintains a diffuse cytoplasmic distribution in unperturbed cells.
source: We observed that ANXA6(FL) maintains a diffuse cytoplasmic distribution in unperturbed cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Upon addition of ionomycin, ANXA6(FL) was recruited to both the plasma membrane and to intracellular vesicles, a portion of which were CD63-positive.
source: However, upon addition of ionomycin, ANXA6(FL) was recruited to both the plasma membrane (as indicated by wheat germ agglutinin [WGA] counterstain) and to intracellular vesicles, a portion of which were CD63-positive (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Upon ionomycin treatment, ANXA6(N), but not ANXA6(C) was recruited to the cell periphery, relative to the WGA counterstain.
source: Upon ionomycin treatment, we observed recruitment of ANXA6(N), but not ANXA6(C) to the cell periphery, relative to the WGA counterstain (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: ANXA6(C) became enriched at intracellular membrane structures, a portion of which were positive for CD63.
source: In contrast to ANXA6(N), we observed that ANXA6(C) became enriched at intracellular membrane structures, a portion of which were positive for CD63 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Exosome secretion is coupled to Ca2+-dependent plasma membrane repair.
source: Our results suggest that exosome secretion is coupled to Ca2+-dependent plasma membrane repair in HCT116 and HEK293T cells (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary claim based on multiple experimental results presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: ANXA6 is recruited to MVBs in the presence of Ca2+.
source: Targeted proteomics was used to demonstrate that ANXA6 is recruited to MVBs in the presence of Ca2+.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: ANXA6 is required for Ca2+-dependent exosome secretion, both in intact and permeabilized cells.
source: We show, both in intact and permeabilized cells, that ANXA6 is required for Ca2+-dependent exosome secretion.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: ANXA6 depletion stalls MVBs at the cell periphery upon Ca2+ ionophore treatment.
source: We then provide evidence that that ANXA6 depletion stalls MVBs at the cell periphery upon Ca2+ ionophore treatment.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Truncations of ANXA6 are enriched at different cellular membranes upon cytosolic Ca2+ elevation.
source: Finally, we demonstrate that truncations of ANXA6 are enriched at different cellular membranes upon cytosolic Ca2+ elevation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Both MVBs and lysosomes undergo Ca2+-dependent exocytosis during plasma membrane repair, resulting in the concurrent secretion of exosomes.
source: Given our findings, we propose that both MVBs and lysosomes undergo Ca2+-dependent exocytosis during plasma membrane repair, resulting in the concurrent secretion of exosomes (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: ANXA6 is directly involved in tethering an MVB to the plasma membrane during exocytosis.
source: Our data favors a model where ANXA6 is directly involved in tethering an MVB to the plasma membrane during exocytosis.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on multiple experimental observations including ANXA6 recruitment to MVBs, stalling of MVBs at the periphery upon ANXA6 depletion, and differential localization of ANXA6 domains.

claim: The two annexin domains of ANXA6 may serve to dock MVBs to the plasma membrane.
source: These two domains may serve to dock MVBs to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the observation that the two domains localize to different membranes upon Ca2+ influx.

claim: In rats, 6.5% of cells in the vascular endothelium of the aorta undergo plasma membrane repair at a given time.
source: In rats, 6.5% of cells in the vascular endothelium of the aorta undergo plasma membrane repair at a given time (Yu and McNeil, 1992); 20% of muscle cells repair their membrane after muscle contractions (McNeil and Khakee, 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Yu and McNeil, 1992.

claim: 20% of muscle cells repair their membrane after muscle contractions.
source: In rats, 6.5% of cells in the vascular endothelium of the aorta undergo plasma membrane repair at a given time (Yu and McNeil, 1992); 20% of muscle cells repair their membrane after muscle contractions (McNeil and Khakee, 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to McNeil and Khakee, 1992.

claim: Exercise stimulates the release of EV-associated proteins and myokines into circulating plasma.
source: Interestingly, Whitham, 2018 demonstrated that exercise stimulates the release of EV-associated proteins and myokines into circulating plasma (Whitham, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Whitham, 2018.

claim: Exosomes act as 'decoys' for pore-forming toxins such as α-toxin.
source: Alternatively, a recent study showed that exosomes act as 'decoys' for pore-forming toxins such as α-toxin (Keller et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Keller et al., 2020.

claim: During staphylococcus infection, cells upregulate exosome production.
source: During staphylococcus infection, cells upregulate exosome production.
evidence: This claim is based on the study by Keller et al., 2020 mentioned in the previous sentence.

claim: SLO binds exosomes at concentrations that may compete with plasma membrane binding.
source: Correspondingly, we find that SLO binds exosomes at concentrations that may compete with plasma membrane binding (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Microinjection studies in echinoderm eggs were the first to demonstrate that metazoan cells repair wounds to the plasma membrane and that this repair process is dependent upon the presence of extracellular Ca2+.
source: Microinjection studies in echinoderm eggs were the first to demonstrate that metazoan cells repair wounds to the plasma membrane and that this repair process is dependent upon the presence of extracellular Ca2+ (Chambers, 1917; Heilbrunn, 1930a; Heilbrunn, 1930b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chambers, 1917; Heilbrunn, 1930a; Heilbrunn, 1930b.

claim: The addition of a Ca2+ ionophore elicited the fusion of plasma membrane-proximal lysosomes with little or no evidence of involvement of early endosomes, late endosomes/MVBs, or vesicles derived from either the endoplasmic reticulum or Golgi apparatus.
source: In their studies, the addition of a Ca2+ ionophore elicited the fusion of plasma membrane-proximal lysosomes with little or no evidence of involvement of early endosomes, late endosomes/MVBs, or vesicles derived from either the endoplasmic reticulum or Golgi apparatus.
evidence: This claim is based on the work of Jaiswal et al., 2002 mentioned in the previous sentence.

claim: The markers used by Jaiswal et al., 2002 to differentiate between late endosomes (Rab7) and lysosomes (CD63) have now been demonstrated to be present in both membrane compartments.
source: The markers used by Jaiswal et al., 2002 to differentiate between late endosomes (Rab7) and lysosomes (CD63) have now been demonstrated to be present in both membrane compartments (Humphries et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Humphries et al., 2011.

claim: Ca2+-dependent plasma membrane repair of sea urchin eggs after micropuncture with glass micropipettes has been demonstrated to be both fusion- and microtubule-dependent as suggested by sensitivity to either botulinum toxins or antibodies that block kinesin-mediated microtubule transport.
source: Ca2+-dependent plasma membrane repair of sea urchin eggs after micropuncture with glass micropipettes has been demonstrated to be both fusion- and microtubule-dependent as suggested by sensitivity to either botulinum toxins or antibodies that block kinesin-mediated microtubule transport (Ingold et al., 1988; Poulain et al., 1988; Schiavo et al., 1992; Steinhardt et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ingold et al., 1988; Poulain et al., 1988; Schiavo et al., 1992; Steinhardt et al., 1994.

claim: Endosomes pre-loaded with Alexa-488-conjugated transferrin traffic toward the plasma membrane upon treatment of cytotoxic T lymphocytes with perforin.
source: Endosomes pre-loaded with Alexa-488-conjugated transferrin traffic toward the plasma membrane upon treatment of cytotoxic T lymphocytes with perforin (Keefe et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Keefe et al., 2005.

claim: Annexin proteins are known to be required for plasma membrane repair.
source: Annexin proteins are known to be required for plasma membrane repair (Blazek et al., 2015; Bouter et al., 2015; Boye and Nylandsted, 2016; Croissant et al., 2021; Gerke and Moss, 2002; Koerdt et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Blazek et al., 2015; Bouter et al., 2015; Boye and Nylandsted, 2016; Croissant et al., 2021; Gerke and Moss, 2002; Koerdt et al., 2019.

claim: Depletion of ANXA6 compromises plasma membrane repair.
source: Depletion of ANXA6 compromises plasma membrane repair, and the N-terminal domain of ANXA6 is insufficient for membrane repair (Croissant et al., 2020; Potez et al., 2011; Swaggart et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Croissant et al., 2020; Potez et al., 2011; Swaggart et al., 2014.

claim: The N-terminal domain of ANXA6 is insufficient for membrane repair.
source: Depletion of ANXA6 compromises plasma membrane repair, and the N-terminal domain of ANXA6 is insufficient for membrane repair (Croissant et al., 2020; Potez et al., 2011; Swaggart et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Croissant et al., 2020; Potez et al., 2011; Swaggart et al., 2014.

claim: ANXA6 is recruited to a peripheral 'repair cap' that is formed at the site of plasma membrane lesions.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that ANXA6 is recruited to a peripheral 'repair cap' that is formed at the site of plasma membrane lesions (Demonbreun et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Demonbreun et al., 2016.

claim: ANXA6 has been demonstrated to tether liposomes in vitro in the presence of Ca2+.
source: ANXA6 has also been demonstrated to tether liposomes in vitro in the presence of Ca2+ (Buzhynskyy et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Buzhynskyy et al., 2009.

claim: The annexin isoform ANXA11 serves as a molecular tether that allows RNA granules to 'hitchhike' on moving lysosomes for their transport.
source: Additionally, a recent study has demonstrated that the annexin isoform ANXA11 serves as a molecular tether that allows RNA granules to 'hitchhike' on moving lysosomes for their transport (Liao et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Liao et al., 2019.

claim: ANXA2 and CPNE3 were both recruited to MVBs and lysosomes in the presence of Ca2+.
source: Although we focused on the role of ANXA6 in Ca2+-dependent exosome secretion, ANXA2 and CPNE3 were both recruited to MVBs and lysosomes in the presence of Ca2+ and knockdown of CPNE3 inhibited MVB exocytosis (Figures 3 and 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 4D.

claim: Knockdown of CPNE3 inhibited MVB exocytosis.
source: Although we focused on the role of ANXA6 in Ca2+-dependent exosome secretion, ANXA2 and CPNE3 were both recruited to MVBs and lysosomes in the presence of Ca2+ and knockdown of CPNE3 inhibited MVB exocytosis (Figures 3 and 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 4D.

claim: Exosomes have potential utility as biomarkers for disease progression because they contain protein and small RNA molecules specific to their cell type of origin.
source: Exosomes have potential utility as biomarkers for disease progression because they contain protein and small RNA molecules specific to their cell type of origin (Driedonks and Nolte-'t Hoen, 2018; Shurtleff et al., 2017; Upton et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Driedonks and Nolte-'t Hoen, 2018; Shurtleff et al., 2017; Upton et al., 2021.

claim: MVBs traffic toward the cell periphery on microtubules or actin filaments.
source: MVBs traffic toward the cell periphery on microtubules or actin filaments (Mittelbrunn et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mittelbrunn et al., 2015.

claim: The influx of extracellular Ca2+ caused by several inducers of plasma membrane lesions triggers exosome secretion and this secretion is dependent on the anterograde trafficking of MVBs on microtubules.
source: We conclude that the influx of extracellular Ca2+ caused by several inducers of plasma membrane lesions triggers exosome secretion and that this secretion is dependent on the anterograde trafficking of MVBs on microtubules.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on multiple experimental results presented in Figure 2.

claim: The modified CD63-Nluc assay faithfully reported the secretion of bona fide CD63-positive exosomes.
source: Thus, our modified CD63-Nluc assay faithfully reported the secretion of bona fide CD63-positive exosomes, and we have used this method to assess the molecular requirements for exosome secretion.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the validation experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Exosomes may participate in intercellular communication.
source: Exosomes may participate in intercellular communication and have utility as disease biomarkers; however, little is known regarding the physiological stimuli that induce their secretion.
evidence: This is a general statement about the potential functions of exosomes, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: Little is known regarding the physiological stimuli that induce exosome secretion.
source: Exosomes may participate in intercellular communication and have utility as disease biomarkers; however, little is known regarding the physiological stimuli that induce their secretion.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field at the time of the study.

claim: Cells secrete exosomes and other EVs upon plasma membrane damage.
source: We find that cells secrete exosomes and other EVs upon plasma membrane damage and propose that repair-induced secretion may contribute to the pool of EVs present within biological fluids.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental results presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Repair-induced secretion may contribute to the pool of EVs present within biological fluids.
source: We find that cells secrete exosomes and other EVs upon plasma membrane damage and propose that repair-induced secretion may contribute to the pool of EVs present within biological fluids.
evidence: This is a proposed hypothesis based on the experimental findings.

claim: ANXA6 may serve as a potential tether for the recruitment of MVBs to the plasma membrane.
source: Our results demonstrate that exosome secretion is coupled to Ca2+-dependent plasma membrane repair and that ANXA6 may serve as a potential tether for the recruitment of MVBs to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Unlike other members of the annexin protein family, ANXA6 contains two complete annexin domains, ANXA6(N) and ANXA6(C).
source: Unlike other members of the annexin protein family, ANXA6 contains two complete annexin domains, ANXA6(N) and ANXA6(C).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the structure of ANXA6.

claim: Endothelium and circulating lymphocytes routinely experience mechanical stress of ~95 dyn/cm2 and transiently experience up to ~3000 dyn/cm2.
source: Endothelium and circulating lymphocytes routinely experience mechanical stress of ~95 dyn/cm2 and transiently experience up to ~3000 dyn/cm2 (Barnes et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Barnes et al., 2012.

claim: ANXA2 is a marker for a subpopulation of plasma membrane-derived EVs.
source: ANXA2 is a marker for a subpopulation of plasma membrane-derived EVs (Jeppesen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Jeppesen et al., 2019.

claim: Treatment of cells with ionomycin for 4 hr did not induce apoptotic cell death.
source: Treatment of cells with ionomycin for 4 hr did not induce apoptotic cell death (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C; Gil-Parrado et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and citation to Gil-Parrado et al., 2002.

claim: SLO treatment of conditioned medium decreased the CD63-Nluc signal when the membrane-impermeable Nluc inhibitor was present.
source: We noted that SLO permeabilized exosomes as well as cells. SLO treatment of conditioned medium decreased the CD63-Nluc signal when the membrane-impermeable Nluc inhibitor was present (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The assay likely underestimates SLO-induced exosome secretion.
source: Thus, our assay likely underestimates SLO-induced exosome secretion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that SLO permeabilizes exosomes.

claim: HEK293T FLAG-Nluc-CD63 cells showed an increase in exosome secretion in a SLO dose- and Ca2+-dependent manner.
source: We observed an increase in FLAG-Nluc-CD63 exosome secretion from this reporter cell line in a SLO dose- and Ca2+-dependent manner (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In the low mechanical stress regime, cells transiently experienced ~89 dyn/cm2 maximum fluid shear stress.
source: In the low mechanical stress regime, cells transiently experienced ~89 dyn/cm2 maximum fluid shear stress, whereas in the high-mechanical stress regime, cells transiently experienced ~178 dyn/cm2 maximum fluid shear stress (Barnes et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the experimental setup and citation to Barnes et al., 2012.

claim: In the high-mechanical stress regime, cells transiently experienced ~178 dyn/cm2 maximum fluid shear stress.
source: In the low mechanical stress regime, cells transiently experienced ~89 dyn/cm2 maximum fluid shear stress, whereas in the high-mechanical stress regime, cells transiently experienced ~178 dyn/cm2 maximum fluid shear stress (Barnes et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the experimental setup and citation to Barnes et al., 2012.

claim: A comparison of ionomycin- and vehicle-treated samples showed drug treatment over equivalent times (4 hr) increased the Nluc luminescence in putative exosome fractions.
source: A comparison of ionomycin- and vehicle-treated samples showed drug treatment over equivalent times (4 hr) increased the Nluc luminescence in putative exosome fractions (Figure 2G, Fraction #10).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The Ca2+ conditional and partial ATP dependence of the reaction may reflect distinct pools of MVBs, some perhaps already bound to the plasma membrane.
source: The Ca2+ conditional and partial ATP dependence of the reaction may reflect distinct pools of MVBs, some perhaps already bound to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental results shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The participation of ANXA6 in the reconstitution was assessed with blocking IgG antibodies targeting epitopes on either GFP or ANXA6.
source: The participation of ANXA6 in the reconstitution was assessed with blocking IgG antibodies targeting epitopes on either GFP or ANXA6.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in Figure 5E.

claim: The results suggest a direct role of ANXA6 in the docking of MVBs at the cell surface.
source: These results suggest a direct role of ANXA6 in the docking of MVBs at the cell surface.
evidence: This is an inference based on the antibody blocking experiments shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Budding of plasma membrane-derived vesicles was observed in the presence of ionomycin.
source: We also observed the budding of plasma membrane-derived vesicles in the presence of ionomycin.
evidence: This is an observation from the microscopy data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Plasma membrane-derived vesicles observed in ionomycin-treated cells may correlate to the low-buoyant density vesicles marked by ANXA2 and FLOT2 that were released from ionomycin-treated cells.
source: These may correlate to the low-buoyant density vesicles marked by ANXA2 and FLOT2 that were released from ionomycin-treated cells (Figure 2F, Fraction #8).
evidence: This is a speculative connection between observations from different experiments.

claim: ANXA6 may serve to tether MVBs to the plasma membrane.
source: ANXA6 depletion stalls MVBs at the cell periphery, and ANXA6 truncations localize to different membranes, suggesting that ANXA6 may serve to tether MVBs to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on multiple experimental observations.
